Residue.code:
/-- Hydrophobic (H) and hydrophilic (P) residues. -/
inductive Residue where
  | H
  | P
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

Sequence.code:
/-- An input protein is a finite word over {H,P}; the empty word is allowed. -/
abbrev Sequence := List Residue

Fold.code:
/-- A self-avoiding walk of length N vertices in an arbitrary simple graph.
Only consecutive positions must be adjacent; other positions may also touch. -/
structure Fold {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (N : ℕ) where
  pos : Fin N → V
  injective_pos : Function.Injective pos
  consecutive : ∀ i j : Fin N, i.val + 1 = j.val → G.Adj (pos i) (pos j)

bondCount.code:
def bondCount (S : Sequence) (f : Fold G S.length) : ℕ :=
  (hhBonds S f).card

HPInstance.Accepts.code:
def HPInstance.Accepts (I : HPInstance) : Prop :=
  HPStringFold (G := cubicLattice) I.sequence I.minBonds

PerfectHPStringFold.code:
/-- A total predicate on raw inputs: an incorrect H count makes it false. -/
def PerfectHPStringFold (S : Sequence) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  hydrophobicCount S = n ^ 3 ∧
    ∃ f : Fold cubicLattice S.length, PacksCube S f n

InNP.code:
/-- The polynomially bounded verifier definition of NP.

The certificate encoder must cover all words over its alphabet. This prevents
an arbitrary encoding image from hiding an undecidable certificate-validity
condition. Ordinary finite-word certificates with `wordEncoding` satisfy this
condition directly. The verifier runs on `pairEncoding ea ec`, whose length is
the input length plus certificate length plus one. Both lengths in the bound
are actual encoding lengths; p has natural coefficients.

This is a predicate definition, not a proof of membership for any HP problem. -/
def InNP {A : Type} (ea : FinEncoding A) (L : A → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (C : Type) (ec : FinEncoding C),
    Function.Surjective ec.encode ∧
    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (R : A × C → Prop),
      PolyTimeDecidable (pairEncoding ea ec) R ∧
        ∀ x, L x ↔ ∃ c, (ec.encode c).length ≤ p.eval (ea.encode x).length ∧ R (x, c)

NPHard.code:
/-- Universal NP-hardness, not hardness relative to an assumed complete problem.
The source type is in universe zero, just as in mathlib's TM2 computation API. -/
def NPHard {A : Type} (ea : FinEncoding A) (L : A → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (B : Type) (eb : FinEncoding B) (M : B → Prop),
    InNP eb M → KarpReduces eb ea M L

KarpReduces.code:
/-- Karp (polynomial-time many-one) reducibility, for independently encoded types.
The reducing function is total and preserves both yes- and no-instances. -/
def KarpReduces {A B : Type} (ea : FinEncoding A) (eb : FinEncoding B)
    (L : A → Prop) (M : B → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : A → B,
    Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea eb f) ∧ ∀ x, L x ↔ M (f x)

hpEncoding.code:
/-- Section 2's HP STRING-FOLD instance with the graph fixed to Z³.
Format: tagged residues, separator, sign bit, binary magnitude of m.
Length = |S| + 2 + bitlength(|m|); no padding and no unary integer field. -/
def hpEncoding : FinEncoding HPInstance :=
  let e := pairEncoding sequenceEncoding signedEncoding
  { Γ := e.Γ
    ΓFin := e.ΓFin
    encode := fun I => e.encode (I.sequence, I.minBonds)
    decode := fun w => (e.decode w).map (fun sm => ⟨sm.1, sm.2⟩)
    decode_encode := by
      intro I
      rw [e.decode_encode]
      cases I
      rfl }

Packing.Instance.code:
structure Instance where
  sizes : List ℕ
  capacity : ℕ
  bins : ℕ
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

Shelf.ExactAccepts.code:
/-- EXACT PACKING. `I.sizes` are the item sizes `a₁, …, a_k`, `I.bins` is `m` and
`I.capacity` is `B`. All of them must be positive; an input that breaks this rule
is a no-instance. -/
def ExactAccepts (I : Packing.Instance) : Prop :=
  Packing.WellFormed I ∧ ∃ parts, Packing.Exact I parts

Shelf.modifiedAccepts_iff.code:
/-- The source problem of the team's library is EXACT PACKING restricted to even
sizes. So our source problem contains theirs, as the paper says. -/
theorem modifiedAccepts_iff (I : Packing.Instance) :
    Packing.ModifiedAccepts I ↔ (∀ s ∈ I.sizes, Even s) ∧ ExactAccepts I

Shelf.normalise.code:
/-- The normalisation of Section 3: multiply every size and the capacity by 6
(`Packing.scale 6`), then make the number of bins odd. -/
def normalise (I : Packing.Instance) : Packing.Instance :=
  padOdd (Packing.scale 6 I)

Shelf.side.code:
/-- The side of the cube, `n = m (B + 1) + 3`. One edge then has `n - 2 = (m + 1) + m B`
inner nodes: room for `m + 1` separators and `m` bins of size `B`. -/
def side (J : Packing.Instance) : ℕ :=
  J.bins * (J.capacity + 1) + 3

Shelf.shelfReduction.code:
/-- The reduction on raw inputs: check the instance, normalise it, write the
string and the side of the cube. -/
def shelfReduction (I : Packing.Instance) : PerfectInput :=
  if Guard I then (shelfWord (normalise I), side (normalise I)) else noInstance

Shelf.hydrophobicCount_shelfWord.code:
/-- Lemma 11, first sentence: the string of a normalised instance has exactly `n³` letters `H`. -/
theorem hydrophobicCount_shelfWord (J : Packing.Instance) (hJ : Normalised J) :
    hydrophobicCount (shelfWord J) = side J ^ 3

Shelf.tether.code:
/-- Lemma 7 (Tether Lemma): if letters `i < j` are `H`'s and all `g = j - i - 1 ≥ 1` letters
between them are `P`'s, then the two sites are at distance at most `g - 1`. -/
theorem tether (hf : Fills S f n) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i + 1 < j)
    (hi : S[i]? = some H) (hj : S[j]? = some H)
    (hP : ∀ t, i < t → t < j → S[t]? = some P) :
    latticeDistance (site f i) (site f j) + 2 ≤ j - i

Shelf.longPath_length_le.code:
/-- Lemma 9, first sentence: a simple path on the skeleton has at most `9n - 10` vertices (`n = d + 2`). -/
theorem longPath_length_le (d : ℕ) (ps : List Site) (hnd : ps.Nodup)
    (hchain : ps.IsChain cubicLattice.Adj) (hsk : ∀ p ∈ ps, EdgeSkeleton 0 (d + 2) p) :
    ps.length ≤ 9 * (d + 2) - 10

Shelf.longPath_free_edges.code:
/-- Lemma 9, second sentence: a simple path with exactly `9n - 10` vertices contains all corners and
all nodes of nine edges, and no two of the three remaining ("free") edges touch. -/
theorem longPath_free_edges (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (ps : List Site) (hnd : ps.Nodup)
    (hchain : ps.IsChain cubicLattice.Adj) (hsk : ∀ p ∈ ps, EdgeSkeleton 0 (d + 2) p)
    (hlen : ps.length = 9 * (d + 2) - 10) :
    ∃ free : Finset CubeEdge, free.card = 3 ∧
      (∀ e ∈ free, ∀ e' ∈ free, e ≠ e' → NoCommonCorner e e') ∧
      (∀ p, p ∈ ps ↔ p ∈ cornerFinset 0 d ∨ ∃ e, e ∉ free ∧ p ∈ openEdgeFinset 0 d e)

Shelf.far_edges.code:
/-- Lemma 10: nodes of two edges that do not touch are at distance at least `n - 1 = d + 1`. -/
theorem far_edges (d : ℕ) {e e' : CubeEdge} (h : NoCommonCorner e e') (r s : Fin d) :
    d + 1 ≤ latticeDistance (openEdgePoint 0 d e r) (openEdgePoint 0 d e' s)

Shelf.far_edges_eq.code:
/-- Lemma 10, the case of equality: the two nodes have the same number on their edges. -/
theorem far_edges_eq (d : ℕ) {e e' : CubeEdge} (h : NoCommonCorner e e') (r s : Fin d)
    (heq : latticeDistance (openEdgePoint 0 d e r) (openEdgePoint 0 d e' s) = d + 1) : r = s

Shelf.far_edges_end.code:
/-- Lemma 10, as used in Step 4: if equality holds and one node is an end node, so is the other. -/
theorem far_edges_end (d : ℕ) {e e' : CubeEdge} (h : NoCommonCorner e e') (r s : Fin d)
    (heq : latticeDistance (openEdgePoint 0 d e r) (openEdgePoint 0 d e' s) = d + 1)
    (hr : IsEnd r) : IsEnd s

Shelf.foldGivesPacking.code:
/-- **Theorem 12.** If the string of a normalised instance has a perfect fold, the
instance has an exact packing. -/
theorem foldGivesPacking : FoldGivesPacking

Shelf.corePath.code:
/-- **Lemma 14 (Core Lemma).** For even `n ≥ 6` there is a path through `n³ - 12n + 16`
different points of the cube that are not on the skeleton, consecutive ones adjacent,
ending at `(1, N, N - 1)`. -/
theorem corePath (n : ℕ) (hn : 6 ≤ n) (heven : Even n) :
    ∃ ps : List Site,
      ps.length = coreLength n ∧ ps.Nodup ∧ ps.IsChain cubicLattice.Adj ∧
      (∀ p ∈ ps, p ∈ Q n ∧ ¬ EdgeSkeleton 0 n p) ∧
      ps.getLast? = some (pt 1 ((n : ℤ) - 1) ((n : ℤ) - 2))

Shelf.routes.code:
/-- **Lemma 15 (Routing Lemma).** `W` is a set of sites with `y ≥ y₀` and `z ≥ z₀`; the ports
`p i`, `q i` have pairwise different `x`-coordinates, and no site of `W` is below a port.
Then the pairs can be joined by pairwise disjoint paths that avoid `W`, the `i`-th one with
`routeBound … + 2 * e i` steps for any prescribed `e i`. We return the inner sites `mid i` of
the paths: the `i`-th path is `p i :: (mid i ++ [q i])`. -/
theorem routes (W : Set Site) (y₀ z₀ : ℤ) (hW : ∀ w ∈ W, y₀ ≤ w 1 ∧ z₀ ≤ w 2)
    (k : ℕ) (p q : Fin k → Site) (e : Fin k → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ i, y₀ ≤ p i 1 ∧ z₀ ≤ p i 2) (hq : ∀ i, y₀ ≤ q i 1 ∧ z₀ ≤ q i 2)
    (hpp : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → p i 0 ≠ p j 0) (hqq : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → q i 0 ≠ q j 0)
    (hpq : ∀ i j, p i 0 ≠ q j 0)
    (hpW : ∀ i, ∀ t : ℤ, 1 ≤ t → pt (p i 0) (p i 1 - t) (p i 2) ∉ W)
    (hqW : ∀ i, ∀ t : ℤ, 1 ≤ t → pt (q i 0) (q i 1 - t) (q i 2) ∉ W) :
    ∃ mid : Fin k → List Site,
      (∀ i, ((mid i).length : ℤ) + 1 = routeBound y₀ z₀ i (p i) (q i) + 2 * (e i : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ i, (p i :: (mid i ++ [q i])).IsChain cubicLattice.Adj) ∧
      (∀ i, (p i :: (mid i ++ [q i])).Nodup) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ s ∈ mid i, s ∉ mid j) ∧
      (∀ i, ∀ s ∈ mid i, s ∉ W) ∧
      (∀ i j, ∀ s ∈ mid i, s ≠ p j ∧ s ≠ q j)

Shelf.layout.code:
/-- The sites of the fold, in the order of the string (Table 1 of the paper). -/
def layout {J : Packing.Instance} (P : Parts J) : List Site :=
  P.core ++ [firstP J] ++ tokSites P.aT ++ ([p₀ J] ++ P.mid 0 ++ [q₀ J, q₀' J]) ++
    tokSites (f₁Tokens J) ++ tether₁ J ++ sepPart J ++ tether₂ J ++ tokSites (f₂Tokens J) ++
    (List.finRange J.sizes.length).flatMap fun i =>
      P.mid i.succ ++ tokSites (itemTokens P.lo i)

Shelf.packingGivesFold.code:
/-- **Theorem 16.** If the instance has an exact packing, the string has a perfect fold. -/
theorem packingGivesFold : PackingGivesFold

Shelf.reductionCorrect.code:
/-- **Theorems 12 and 16 together.** The reduction of the paper is correct on every
input: an input is a yes-instance of EXACT PACKING exactly when its string has a
perfect fold. -/
theorem reductionCorrect : ReductionCorrect

Shelf.shelfMap_polyTime.code:
/-- **Proof of Theorem 1, "this takes polynomial time".** A Turing machine computes
the map in polynomial time, for sizes written in unary: it makes the check
(the team's machine), normalises the instance (`normaliseComputable`), and writes
the string and the side of the cube (`shelfPairComputable`). -/
theorem shelfMap_polyTime :
    Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime Packing.instanceEncoding perfectEncoding shelfMap)

Shelf.shelfKarp.code:
/-- The shelf map is a polynomial-time many-one reduction from the team's source
problem to PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD. -/
theorem shelfKarp :
    KarpReduces Packing.instanceEncoding perfectEncoding Packing.ModifiedAccepts PerfectFolds

hpStringFold_inNP.code:
/-- HP STRING-FOLD on the fixed cubic lattice belongs to NP (footnote 1).
The polynomial verifier is implemented and its soundness/completeness proved. -/
theorem hpStringFold_inNP : InNP hpEncoding (fun I : HPInstance => I.Accepts)

perfectHPStringFold_inNP.code:
/-- PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD belongs to NP (footnote 1). Raw inputs with the
wrong H count are rejected, exactly as in the frozen problem definition. -/
theorem perfectHPStringFold_inNP :
    InNP perfectEncoding (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)

SATPacking.modifiedBinPackingUnary_NPHar.code:
/-- The strong unary packing source is NP-hard assuming only Cook--Levin.
Every reduction and runtime witness used after that source assumption is
proved, rather than supplied as an additional hypothesis. -/
theorem modifiedBinPackingUnary_NPHard (hCL : CookLevin) :
    Packing.ModifiedBinPackingUnaryNPHard

hpNPHard_of_perfectNPHard.code:
theorem hpNPHard_of_perfectNPHard
    (h : NPHard perfectEncoding (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)) :
    NPHard hpEncoding (fun I : HPInstance => I.Accepts)

PerfectHPStringFoldNPHard.code:
/-- The main hardness step, Section 2 and Section 3.2 (pp. 31-32):
PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD is NP-hard. Raw inputs with the wrong H count are rejected. -/
def PerfectHPStringFoldNPHard : Prop :=
  NPHard perfectEncoding (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)

Shelf.perfectHPStringFold_NPHard.code:
/-- **Theorem 1, hardness.** PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD is NP-hard, given the
Cook–Levin theorem. -/
theorem perfectHPStringFold_NPHard (hCL : SAT.CookLevin) : PerfectHPStringFoldNPHard

PerfectHPStringFoldNPComplete.code:
/-- Section 3.2's NP-completeness claim for PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD.
Footnote 1 (p. 31) distinguishes hardness from the additional NP-membership step.
The raw-input formulation uses the same perfect-packing predicate as Section 2. -/
def PerfectHPStringFoldNPComplete : Prop :=
  NPComplete perfectEncoding (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2)

Shelf.perfectHPStringFold_NPComplete.code:
/-- **Theorem 1.** PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD is NP-complete, given the Cook–Levin
theorem. -/
theorem perfectHPStringFold_NPComplete (hCL : SAT.CookLevin) : PerfectHPStringFoldNPComplete

HPStringFoldNPComplete.code:
/-- The paper's main result, announced in Section 2 (p. 31) and Section 3:
HP STRING-FOLD on the fixed cubic lattice Z³ is NP-complete. -/
def HPStringFoldNPComplete : Prop :=
  NPComplete hpEncoding (fun I : HPInstance => I.Accepts)

Shelf.hpStringFold_NPComplete.code:
/-- **Corollary 2.** HP STRING-FOLD on the cubic lattice is NP-complete, given the
Cook–Levin theorem. -/
theorem hpStringFold_NPComplete (hCL : SAT.CookLevin) : HPStringFoldNPComplete

SAT.CookLevin.code:
/-- **The Cook–Levin hypothesis**: CNF-SAT (binary indices) is NP-hard in the
project's sense. Use only as an explicit hypothesis. -/
def CookLevin : Prop := NPHard cnfEncoding Satisfiable

Shelf.PerfectFolds.code:
/-- The predicate of PERFECT HP STRING-FOLD on raw inputs, as in the team's
`PerfectHPStringFoldNPHard`. -/
abbrev PerfectFolds (X : PerfectInput) : Prop :=
  PerfectHPStringFold X.1 X.2

Shelf.PackingGivesFold.code:
/-- **Theorem 16** (a packing gives a perfect fold). If a normalised instance has an
exact packing, its string has a perfect fold. -/
def PackingGivesFold : Prop :=
  ∀ J : Packing.Instance, Normalised J →
    (∃ parts, Packing.Exact J parts) → PerfectHPStringFold (shelfWord J) (side J)

Shelf.FoldGivesPacking.code:
/-- **Theorem 12** (a perfect fold gives a packing). If the string of a normalised
instance has a perfect fold, the instance has an exact packing. -/
def FoldGivesPacking : Prop :=
  ∀ J : Packing.Instance, Normalised J →
    PerfectHPStringFold (shelfWord J) (side J) → ∃ parts, Packing.Exact J parts

Shelf.ReductionCorrect.code:
/-- **Theorems 12 and 16 on raw inputs.** The reduction sends yes-instances to
yes-instances and no-instances to no-instances. -/
def ReductionCorrect : Prop :=
  ∀ I : Packing.Instance, ExactAccepts I ↔ PerfectFolds (shelfReduction I)

SATPacking.cnfToSortedModified_karp.code:
/-- A complete Karp reduction from the unchanged binary-variable CNF language
to positive-even, exact, unary modified packing. -/
theorem cnfToSortedModified_karp :
    KarpReduces cnfEncoding Packing.instanceEncoding Satisfiable Packing.ModifiedAccepts

perfect_karpReduces_hp.code:
/-- Theorem 3.2 yields an actual Karp reduction on all raw perfect inputs.
The wrong-H-count cases map to a fixed HP no-instance. -/
theorem perfect_karpReduces_hp :
    KarpReduces perfectEncoding hpEncoding
      (fun I : PerfectInput => PerfectHPStringFold I.1 I.2) (fun I : HPInstance => I.Accepts)
